inputs.base_revenue_basis: Chemicals business only: FY2026 consolidated continuing-ops revenue 3,703,988 less Industrial Gases segment external revenue 1,352,498 (4188.T_Annual_FY2025.txt segment table, year ended 31 March 2026). The DCF models the chemicals business; the 50.6% Nippon Sanso Holdings (NSHD, 4091.T) stake is carried in equity_bridge at market under the matching-asset rule.
inputs.share_count_basis: 1,441,467,207 issued less 82,779,392 treasury (incl. BIP-trust shares) at 30 June 2026 (4188.T_Quarterly_Q1-2026.txt:94-100). FY2026 diluted weighted average 1,370.9M vs basic 1,370.9M: no dilutive instruments. Held FLAT; SBC is immaterial (BIP trust) and the FY2026 Y50bn buyback is already in the count.
inputs.net_debt_basis: Consolidated, 30 June 2026 (Q1 FY2027): bonds and borrowings 341,070 current + 1,503,983 non-current = 1,845,053 (4188.T_Quarterly_Q1-2026.txt:449,460); lease liabilities 134,547 (company interest-bearing debt 1,979,600 incl. leases less bonds/borrowings); cash 445,086 (line 419). Lease treatment (A): leases held as debt, so net_debt = 1,845,053 + 134,547 - 445,086 = 1,534,514. The portion belonging to the Industrial Gases sub-group (NSHD net debt ~701,810) is added back in equity_bridge because NSHD is valued at market, not through the flows.
inputs.reported_fcf_basis: Chemicals-only FY2026 derived: consolidated OCF 436,287 less NSHD OCF 272,594 (securities report note 38 summary) = 163,693; less chemicals cash capex ~178,888 (consolidated PPE 284,089 + intangibles 8,044 = 292,133 less NSHD segment capex 113,245). Consolidated reported FCF per Metrics.csv is 152,198 (OCF less PPE capex); consolidated owner FCF ex-intangibles and SBC is 144,094. The chemicals figure includes a small discontinued-ops (pharma, Q1-Q2 FY2026) contribution that cannot be separated in the filings, so the true ex-pharma chemicals trough FCF was somewhat lower.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2026 consolidated statement of changes in equity, share-based payment transactions Y60M (4188.T_Annual_FY2025.txt:674); BIP-trust performance shares only. SBC-zero market: house and street coincide, band_position null.
inputs.interest_income_note: FY2026 interest income Y9,220M (interest received Y4,663M) left in the flows and NOT stripped: the group carries ~Y1.5tn of net debt, so there is no cash pile to double-count.
inputs.buyback_note: FY2026 purchase of treasury stock Y50,025M (4188.T_Annual_FY2025.txt:670); Q1 FY2027 nil. Value-neutral in this model (count held flat).
inputs.fy_label_note: END-year convention throughout: FY2026 = year ended 31 March 2026 (the company's own materials call this 'FY2025'). Year 1 of the projection = FY2027 (year ending 31 March 2027, the current guidance year).
inputs.wacc_rationale: Built in JPY, the currency of the flows. 10y JGB ~1.7% + 6.0% ERP x beta ~1.15 = cost of equity ~8.6%; pre-tax cost of debt ~1.9% (FY2026 interest paid Y36.7bn on ~Y2.0tn), ~1.3% after tax; chemicals-attributable net debt ~Y0.83tn against ~Y1.2tn implied chemicals equity gives D/V ~40% and a mechanical WACC near 5.7%. House uses 7.0% as the floor for a JPY commodity-exposed cyclical with Y0.8tn of attributable net debt. Same WACC in all three scenarios: cyclicality, MMA overcapacity and execution risk are charged once, in the scenario flows and weights, not again in the rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: (A) Leases as debt. IFRS 16 lease liabilities (134,547 at 30 June 2026) are inside net_debt; lease principal (FY2026 32,588) is NOT deducted from the flows; segment D&A (which includes right-of-use depreciation, FY2026 consolidated ROU depreciation 28,620 per securities report note 34) is used as da_pct, and segment capital expenditures (which include ROU additions) as capex_pct, so the lease asset renewal is charged through the capex line. lease_cost_pct_path is 0 by construction, not omission.
inputs.nci_treatment: Charged once, via the bridge. Non-controlling interests are Y679,441M at 30 June 2026 (Q1 filing line 475), of which NSHD is ~94% (Y615,543M of Y653,005M at 31 March 2026, securities report note 38; NCI percentage 49.4%). Because NSHD is a listed, liquid Y2.4tn company, the consolidated DCF is NOT used for it: the Industrial Gases flows are excluded from the projection (base_revenue, margins, D&A and capex are chemicals-only), MCG's 50.6% stake is added to the bridge at market, NSHD's own net debt (inside consolidated net_debt) is added back, and the remaining non-NSHD NCI (~Y39bn) is deducted at book. Deducting the NSHD minority at market from a consolidated DCF would instead have charged MCG shareholders for the whole gap between the market's valuation of gases and the DCF's.
inputs.equity_method_note: Chemicals-segment equity-method investments (~Y83bn book) are left out of the bridge because their share of profit (FY2026 -Y6.9bn) sits inside segment core operating income and therefore inside the modelled flows.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF DCF (component engine), applied to the CHEMICALS business (Specialty Materials, MMA & Derivatives, Basic Materials & Polymers, Others, corporate) on the continuing-operations basis, plus the 50.6% NSHD stake at market -- a sum-of-parts under adaptation (d) of owner-fcf-adaptations.md. Routing: SKILL.md row 2 (operating company, non-US, cyclical) -> owner-fcf.md + adaptations. Reasons: (1) Mitsubishi Tanabe Pharma was sold to Bain in FY2026 (~Y510bn); FY2025 was restated to 3,947,566 continuing revenue and FY2026 is the first clean ex-pharma year, so projections compound from FY2026 continuing-ops figures and pre-divestiture history is not used for the base. (2) FY2026 chemicals core operating income of Y24.3bn (0.8% consolidated operating margin after Y195bn of non-core impairments/exit costs) is a trough; the base case normalises to a mid-cycle chemicals core OI of ~Y85bn in FY2027 (guidance Y100bn less the management-quantified ~Y18bn Strait of Hormuz risk) rising to ~Y140bn by FY2031, roughly 60% of the MTMP2029 Y236bn target, and charges a recurring ~1.0% of revenue (~Y25bn/yr) for the restructuring/impairment cash costs this company books almost every year (statutory operating income has trailed core by Y150-195bn in each of the last two years). (3) Industrial Gases (~Y200bn core OI, 65% of group profit) is valued through the NSHD market price rather than through the chemicals DCF's cyclical terminal cap. EBITDA margin paths are CORE operating income + segment D&A, net of the non-core charge, as a % of chemicals revenue (FY2026 actual 6.9% before the charge). Capex path starts from FY2026 chemicals segment capex of 8.3% of revenue (Specialty Materials alone 12%: precision cleaning, EUV precursor, synthetic silica, films build-out) and declines as management moves 'from defence to offence' with those projects in full operation. SBC-zero market. A 10% holding-company discount on the NSHD stake, not applied, would be worth ~Y89/share.
inputs.nshd_stake_valuation: NSHD 432.85M shares outstanding (stockanalysis.com, 2026-10-31) x Y5,506 (Yahoo 4091.T regular close 2026-10-30) = market cap Y2,383,272M; MCG 50.6% = Y1,205,936M; minority 49.4% at market = Y1,177,336M vs ~Y640bn book NCI. NSHD net debt Y701,810M (total debt Y868,460M incl. leases less cash, stockanalysis.com latest quarter, 2026-10-31 fetch).

equity_bridge.note: 432.85M sh x Y5,506 x 50.6%; NSHD is a listed subsidiary whose flows are excluded from the chemicals DCF (matching-asset rule). NCI percentage 49.4% per securities report note 38.

equity_bridge.note: NSHD total debt Y868.5bn incl. leases less cash Y166.7bn (stockanalysis.com, latest quarter). The gases business' debt is already priced in the NSHD market value above; leaving it in consolidated net_debt would deduct it twice.

equity_bridge.item: Non-controlling interests other than NSHD, at book
equity_bridge.note: Total NCI 679,441 at 30 June 2026 less NSHD share (~94% per 31 March 2026 split 615,543 / 653,005).

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: judgment: chemicals continuing-operations long-run growth (specialty materials growth net of basic-materials/cracker shrinkage); historical consolidated CAGRs are not usable because of the pharma divestiture
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Reported CAGRs are on the CONSOLIDATED series and are distorted by the FY2026 pharma divestiture (revenue 3-yr FY2023 4,634,532 -> FY2026 3,703,988 includes ~Y440bn of pharma leaving; 5-yr FY2021 3,257,535 -> 3,703,988 is +2.6% reported, ~+5% ex-pharma). Equity 3/5-yr: 1,564,366 -> 1,761,675 (+4.0%), 1,236,339 -> 1,761,675 (+7.3%), parent-only, lifted by the pharma sale gain and weak-yen translation. Owner FCF (consolidated, OCF less PPE and intangibles capex, treatment A): FY2021 ~200,700 -> FY2023 74,194 -> FY2026 144,094; 3-yr +24.8%, 5-yr -6.4%: noise, not trend. EPS 3-yr/5-yr not meaningful (FY2021 -5.32, FY2026 8.63 after Y195bn non-core charges).
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF CAGRs use OCF - PPE capex - intangibles capex - SBC; SBC is ~zero so adjusted and reported series coincide. The chemicals-only series needed for this DCF cannot be reconstructed before FY2025 (segment cash flows are not disclosed), which is why selected_growth_rate is a forward judgment rather than a historical CAGR.

base.growth_note: FY2027 +3.5% to ~Y2,434bn: consolidated guidance Y3,800bn less NSHD ~Y1,400bn implies ~+2%, Q1 FY2027 chemicals revenue ran +17% YoY on MMA/naphtha price spikes and yen weakness; thereafter ~1%/yr as Specialty Materials growth is offset by Basic Materials shrinkage (Western Japan cracker consolidation by 2030).
base.margin_note: EBITDA = chemicals core operating income + segment D&A, less ~1.0pp recurring non-core restructuring/impairment cash cost. FY2026 actual 6.9% gross (core OI 24.3bn + D&A 138.4bn on 2,351.5bn). Y1 8.3% net = 9.3% gross = core OI ~Y83bn (guidance Y100bn less ~Y18bn Hormuz risk). Y5 10.5% net = 11.5% gross = core OI ~Y143bn, ~60% of the MTMP2029 Y236bn target; mature 11.0% net.
base.capex_note: FY2026 chemicals segment capex 195.6bn = 8.3% of revenue, the peak of the growth build-out; declines to 6.3% (D&A 5.9% incl. ROU depreciation + ~1% growth) as the large projects enter full operation. Includes ROU additions under lease treatment (A).
base.tax_note: 30% cash tax: Japanese statutory ~30.6%, chemicals mostly Japan-taxed, no material loss carryforward benefit assumed.
base.wc_note: Manufacturer with receivables + inventories > payables: growth consumes ~15% of the revenue increase.
base.terminal_note: Terminal growth 1.0% nominal JPY; cap 14x owner FCF (between the 12x cyclical and 20x compounder caps: ~55% of chemicals EBITDA is Specialty Materials, ~45% MMA/basic commodity). At terminal FCF the 14x cap equals ~3.9x EBITDA, well below listed chemicals peers at 6-7x, which is the honest consequence of capex consuming most of EBITDA.

bull.margin_note: Non-core charge halves to 0.5pp. Y1 9.5% net = 10.0% gross = FY2027 guidance of Y100bn chemicals core OI delivered with no Middle East hit; Y5 13.6% net = 14.1% gross = core OI ~Y233bn on ~Y2.84tn revenue, i.e. the MTMP2029 Y236bn target reached one year late (FY2031 end-year = company 'FY2030').

bear.margin_note: Non-core charge persists at 1.5pp (another Soarnol/EO-EG/MMA-Europe-sized write-down and exit every year or two). Y1 7.5% net = 9.0% gross = core OI ~Y74bn (guidance missed on Hormuz and MMA); gross margin never exceeds 9.8% = core OI stuck at ~Y90bn, below the Y100bn guided for FY2027 and nowhere near the MTMP target. Capex stays above D&A as the semiconductor build-out keeps needing money.

scenario_narratives.base: The chemicals turnaround is real but partial. Specialty Materials (semiconductor precision cleaning, EUV resist precursor, synthetic silica, films, composites) grows into its FY2024-26 capex and lifts chemicals core operating income from the FY2026 trough of Y24bn to ~Y85bn in FY2027 (guidance Y100bn less the ~Y18bn Strait of Hormuz exposure management itself quantified) and ~Y140bn by FY2031 -- about 60% of the MTMP2029 Y236bn target, consistent with this company's record of under-delivering on plans. MMA returns to modest profit on European/Taiwan restructuring but Chinese overcapacity caps the spread; Basic Materials shrinks toward breakeven as the three-company Western Japan cracker consolidation lands around 2030. Capex falls from 8.3% of revenue to ~6.3% as the growth projects enter full operation, which is where most of the FCF improvement comes from. A ~Y25bn/yr non-core restructuring cash cost is charged every year because statutory results have trailed core results by Y150-195bn in each of the last two years. Industrial Gases is valued at NSHD's market price, so gases growth is in the price, not the flows.
scenario_narratives.bull: 'From defence to offence' works. The MTMP2029 chemicals core OI target of Y236bn is reached one year late (FY2031 end-year basis) as semiconductor/AI-driven demand for precision cleaning, EUV precursors and synthetic silica compounds at double-digit rates, composites win new mobility and aerospace programmes, MMA spreads recover with Chinese capacity discipline, and the petrochemicals spin-off/cracker alliance removes the loss-making tail. Non-core charges fall to half a point of revenue, capex normalises to D&A plus growth, and no Middle East disruption hits FY2027. Revenue grows 3-5% through FY2031. Even here the terminal multiple is capped at 15x FCF (~4.1x EBITDA), so the bull is a cash-flow bull, not a re-rating bull.
scenario_narratives.bear: China structural overcapacity in MMA and basic petrochemicals never clears, the Asian spread stays at or below cost, and the FY2027 guidance is missed on the Hormuz disruption and a weaker-than-guided MMA recovery. Chemicals core OI plateaus around Y90bn, below even the FY2027 guidance, while the company keeps booking Soarnol-, coke/carbon- and EO/EG-sized impairments and exit costs (1.5% of revenue a year) and keeps spending above D&A on the semiconductor build-out. Revenue drifts flat to slightly down as crackers close. The chemicals business is then worth little more than its net debt; the equity value is essentially the NSHD stake less the chemicals-attributable debt, and the group's ~Y0.8tn of chemicals net debt leaves no margin for a second lost decade.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear lifted from the 15% default to 25%: the company has booked large impairments or exit charges in each of the last four years, missed its own FY2026 forecast in October 2025, carries Y0.8tn of chemicals-attributable net debt, and its two commodity segments face a structural Chinese overcapacity overhang with no visible end. Bull cut from 35% to 25%: it needs the MTMP2029 chemicals target, an MMA spread recovery, a clean petrochemicals carve-out and no Middle East disruption to all come through together, and management guided FY2027 excluding the Hormuz risk it quantified. Base 50%: FY2027 guidance roughly delivered net of Hormuz, and a partial, delayed MTMP delivery.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Sum-of-parts: an owner-FCF DCF of the chemicals business on the continuing-operations (ex-pharma) basis, normalised from the FY2026 trough to a mid-cycle chemicals core operating income with a recurring charge for the restructuring costs this company books almost every year, plus MCG's 50.6% stake in listed Nippon Sanso Holdings at market and NSHD's net debt added back. The chemicals DCF is deliberately a cash-flow valuation: the terminal cap of 12-15x owner FCF equals only ~3.5-4x EBITDA because capex absorbs most of chemicals EBITDA, so the valuation does not grant the 6-7x EV/EBITDA that listed chemicals peers trade on. The market price therefore implies either that chemicals FCF conversion improves beyond the base path or that the MTMP2029 target is largely delivered.
key_risks_to_valuation: NSHD stake at market: the single largest component of value (~Y890/share gross) moves with 4091.T, not with anything MCG controls; a 10% de-rating of NSHD or a holding-company discount costs ~Y89/share.
Mid-cycle normalisation: the base assumes FY2027 chemicals core OI of ~Y83bn against a FY2026 actual of Y24bn; if FY2026 was not a trough but the new normal, the bear case applies.
Recurring non-core charges: the 1.0pp/yr charge is a judgment; the last two years ran 4-5x that in statutory terms (mostly non-cash impairments).
Capex normalisation: most of the FCF improvement comes from capex falling from 8.3% to 6.3% of revenue, not from margins; a second growth build-out would push the base toward the bear.
Chemicals-only cash flows before FY2025 are not disclosed, so FY0 FCF and the 'mid-cycle' anchor are derived from segment core OI, D&A and capex rather than observed.
Strait of Hormuz / Middle East: guidance excludes it; management's own estimate is ~Y18bn of FY2027 core OI if disruption persisted through September 2026.
Terminal multiple: at 14x FCF the chemicals terminal value is ~3.9x EBITDA; every 1x of FCF multiple is ~Y40/share.
